chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who inherited wealth while the man was absent; is Zakat obligatory upon him? He said, 'No, until he arrives.' I said, 'Does he pay Zakat when he arrives?' He said, 'No, until a full year passes over it.'

key_terms.يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: A full year passes over it

ai.seo_question: When does the Zakat year begin for inherited wealth if the heir is absent?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'Hawl' (lunar year) for Zakat is applied specifically to inherited wealth, establishing that the obligation does not trigger immediately upon death of the deceased but rather begins once the heir takes actual possession upon their return. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that Zakat is tied to the holder's control and the completion of a full lunar year from the moment of effective ownership, distinguishing it from immediate liability. It underscores the practical ease granted to heirs, ensuring they are not burdened with Zakat calculations during periods of absence or transition.
